MINOR: Moving `Close()` from `defer` to an explicit post-shutdown call means a panic between auditor construction and shutdown no longer flushes the audit queue (a `defer` would have run during unwind); consider keeping a `defer` as a backstop alongside the ordered explicit call.

`TestMemoryAuditLifecycle` asserts no observable outcome (no `memory_audit_dropped_total` increment, no record-in-store check), and the channel-full drop path with the 50ms timer remains untested, so the delta's core drop/shutdown behavior can regress undetected.

The drop path logs one unbounded line per dropped event with no rate limiting; under the same burst that fills the channel this can flood logs and degrade the observability needed to diagnose the loss.

`Audit` holds `mu.RLock()` across a blocking send of up to 50ms, so `Close()` (and thus shutdown) can be stalled by up to 50ms per in-flight audit under a full channel; bounded but worth documenting as an accepted shutdown-latency cost.
NIT: The `50 * time.Millisecond` backoff is a hard-coded magic duration with no rationale or configurability; derive it from the /memory latency budget or document why 50ms is the accepted bound.
`TestMemoryAuditLifecycle` is a smoke test with no `-race`-specific concurrency coverage of `Audit` racing `Close`; a concurrent variant would pin the new `closed`/`mu` guard under the race detector.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly resolves the prior panic-on-closed-channel MAJOR (closed-state guard under RLock held across send), the shutdown-ordering MINOR (explicit `Close()` before `st.Close()`), and the drop-log correlation MINOR (actor/record added); prior drop-on-full MAJOR remains validly PENDING since events can still be dropped after the 50ms wait.
No AC-1/AC-2/AC-3 regression introduced by this delta; residual risk is audit-integrity under burst load and weak assertion coverage of the new lifecycle/drop paths.
Top risks: untested channel-full drop path, panic-path audit flush loss from the defer removal, and per-event log flooding during degradation.
